_note: Sticky notes for the Culture layer. Text is paraphrased from the source page; no invented facts. approx=true means the pin position is an estimate that a human must check.

notes.title: Freshman Cake Race
notes.text: Homecoming morning, before sunrise, freshmen run half a mile and finish on top of Freshman Hill by Bobby Dodd. Everybody gets cupcakes, the winners get actual cakes. Not required anymore, but they really want you there.
notes.tip: Ramblin' Reck Club bakes the cupcakes the night before.
notes.where: Finish line on top of Freshman Hill, by Bobby Dodd
facts: First run in 1911 as an open cross-country race.
The name comes from faculty wives baking cakes for the winners.
Freshmen were required to run from 1935; now it's just strongly encouraged.
At halftime Mr. and Ms. Georgia Tech kiss the winners on the field.
The course is half a mile long.

notes.title: Mini 500
notes.text: Tricycle race around Peters Parking Deck, Friday afternoon before the Homecoming game. Teams of seven: four drivers, three pit crew. Running since 1969, run by Ramblin' Reck Club.
notes.tip: Go watch at least once. It's chaotic in the best way.
notes.when: Friday afternoon before the Homecoming game
facts: Grew out of a 1960s fraternity prank where pledges rode tricycles around campus.
Each team goes for 8 laps.

notes.title: The Ramblin' Reck
notes.text: A 1930 Ford Model A that leads the football team onto the field at every home game, since Sept. 30, 1961. Cared for by Ramblin' Reck Club and an elected Reck Driver.
notes.tip: Home game days: look for it at Bobby Dodd.
notes.where: Leads the team onto the field at Bobby Dodd
facts: A 1930 Ford Model A Sport Coupe in Old Gold and White.
First led the team out on Sept. 30, 1961 (Tech beat Rice 24-0).

notes.title: Ramblin' Wreck Parade
notes.text: Homecoming Saturday morning, last event before the game. The Reck leads it, starting at McCamish Pavilion and ending at Ferst and Fowler. Fixed bodies, classic cars and human-powered contraptions. Started in 1932 after the old Atlanta-to-Athens car race got deemed unsafe.
notes.when: Homecoming Saturday morning, last event before the game
notes.where: McCamish Pavilion to Ferst and Fowler
facts: Began as the Old Ford Race (Atlanta to Athens) in 1929 and 1930.
Deemed unsafe in 1932, so the parade took its place.
Skipped in 1942 and 1943 for WWII gas shortages.
Three categories today: fixed bodies, classic cars, contraptions (human-powered).

notes.title: Goldfellas
notes.text: The painted-body super fans at every home football game. The walk starts at the Howey building half an hour before kickoff (the March), chants at Techwood and Bobby Dodd Way (the Chant), then sprints to the south gate of Bobby Dodd (the Run). First showed up at Homecoming 1998.
notes.where: March from Howey, chant at Techwood and Bobby Dodd Way, run to the south gate
facts: First appeared at Homecoming 1998 vs. Virginia (Tech won 41-38).
The walk has three phases: the March, the Chant, the Run.

notes.title: George P. Burdell
notes.text: Our most famous student who never existed. Enrolled in 1927 as a prank, supposedly graduated in mechanical engineering in 1930. In 1969 students registered him for every class by hacking registration. You will hear his name for four years.
facts: A prank by William Edgar Smith in 1927, who enrolled George P. Burdell from Richmond Academy in Augusta.
Supposedly earned a BS in Mechanical Engineering in 1930.
In 1969 students hacked registration to sign him up for every class (3,000+ hours).
Registered again in 1975 and 1980.

notes.title: The Whistle
notes.text: Blows five minutes before the hour, 8am to 6pm on weekdays, so you know you're late. Oldest recorded tradition at Tech (1892). Also blows for touchdowns. It's been stolen before, famously the night before the president's 1995 inauguration.
notes.tip: You'll set your walk to class by it.
notes.when: Five minutes before the hour, 8am to 6pm on weekdays
facts: Oldest recorded tradition at Tech: first steam whistle in 1892 in the rebuilt Shop Building.
First stolen in 1905.
Stolen May 12, 1995, the night before G. Wayne Clough's inauguration.
Current one built by GTRI in 2004; also blows for touchdowns and home wins.
The When the Whistle Blows ceremony honors people who died in the past year.

notes.title: Buzz
notes.text: The Yellow Jacket mascot. Heisman made the Yellow Jackets official in 1905. Buzz first showed up on the sideline in 1980. Students play Buzz and keep their identity secret until graduation.
facts: In 1905 John Heisman declared the team the Yellow Jackets.
Judy McNair performed as a human Yellow Jacket from 1972.
Buzz debuted with the cheerleaders on Oct. 11, 1980; Rickie Bland was the first official Buzz.
Performers keep their identity secret until graduation.

notes.title: Rat Caps
notes.text: Freshman caps since 1915, handed out at Convocation. Football scores get written on the panels, and the back says something unkind about a certain Georgia school.
notes.tip: Keep yours, you'll want it in four years.
facts: Caps date back to 1915 (originally white-F freshman caps).
Football scores get written on the panels.
The back panel reads To HELL with georgia.
RAT rules ended under anti-hazing policies.

notes.title: Clean Old-Fashioned Hate
notes.text: The rivalry with UGA. First game 1893. The Ramblin' Wreck fight song was born out of Georgia fans harassing Tech fans that year. Tech beat them 51-48 in overtime in 1999.
notes.tip: Do not wear red and black on the Green.
facts: First game on Nov. 4, 1893 in Athens: Tech won 28-6.
UGA fans harassing Tech fans that year inspired the Ramblin' Wreck fight song.
Series record per the Reck Club: 41 wins, 67 losses, 5 ties.
Most recent Tech win they list: 2016, 28-27. The 1999 overtime win was 51-48.

notes.title: T-Book
notes.text: The freshman guide, handed out at Convocation. Started by the YMCA, ran 65+ years, came back in print in 2008 from Ramblin' Reck Club.
facts: Originally published by the GT YMCA; ran 65+ years and stopped in 1970.
Brought back as a website in 1997, in print in 2008 by Ramblin' Reck Club.
2,673 copies went out at the 2013 convocation.

notes.title: The 'Nique
notes.text: The student newspaper since November 1911. Special issues like To Hell With Georgia, Freshman and Best of Tech.
notes.when: Weekly fall and spring, biweekly summer
facts: First issue on Nov. 17, 1911.
Special issues: To Hell With Georgia, Freshman and Best of Tech.

notes.title: GT songs
notes.text: Up With the White and Gold (1919), the Budweiser Song between the 3rd and 4th quarters, and The Horse when the band closes out a game. Learn them before your first game.
notes.tip: Sing loud on the Budweiser Song.
facts: Up With the White and Gold was released in 1919; Frank Roman wrote it.
Reportedly Nixon and Khrushchev sang it together in Moscow in 1959.
The Budweiser Song plays between the 3rd and 4th quarters.
The Horse ends every event where the band plays.
